### assuming outliers exists. Then 
## we handle outliers using 1.5 IQR rule
```{r}
Q1<-quantile(kl$ExamScore, 0.25)
Q3<-quantile(kl$ExamScore, 0.75)
IQR<- Q3-Q1
lower_bound<-Q1-1.5*IQR
upper_bound<-Q3+1.5*IQR
cp<-kl[kl$ExamScore >= lower_bound & kl$ExamScore <= upper_bound, ]
```

### mean, median, varaince and standard deviation of the data

```{r}
mean_val<-mean(cp$ExamScore, na.rm=TRUE)
median_val <-median(cp$ExamScore, na.rm=TRUE)
variance_val <-var(cp$ExamScore, na.rm=TRUE)
sd_val<-sd(cp$ExamScore, na.rm=TRUE)
print(paste("mean:", mean_val ))
print(paste("median:", median_val ))
print(paste("variance:", variance_val ))
print(paste("standard deviationincome:", sd_val ))
```

### visualization using scatterplots

## Scatter plot using previusGPA against Age
```{r}
ggplot(cp, aes(x=Age, y=PreviousGPA))+
  geom_point(col="purple", size=2)+
  labs(x="Age of Students",
       y=" previousGPA of Students",
       title="     scatter plot of previusGPA against Age")
```


## Scatter plot using ExamScore against Age
```{r}
ggplot(cp, aes(x=Age, y=ExamScore))+
  geom_point(col="blue", size=2)+
  labs(x="Age of Students",
       y=" ExamScore of Students",
       title="     scatter plot of ExamScore against Age")
```

## Scatter plot using ExamScore against PreviousGPA
